html:
Vladimir-Suzdal was a Rus principality in the forests of the northeast, between the upper Volga and the Oka, from the 1100s to the 1300s. It is on the map for 1200, when it was the strongest of the Rus states.

Yuri Dolgorukiy moved his seat to Suzdal in 1125, and in his time Moscow is first mentioned. His son Andrey Bogolyubsky made Vladimir the capital in 1157, filled it with white stone churches, brought the icon later called the Virgin of Vladimir, and in 1169 sent an army to sack Kyiv. His brother Vsevolod "Big Nest" had so many sons that their lines ruled the northeast for centuries.

In 1238 the Mongols burned Vladimir. Its grand princes, among them Alexander Nevsky, now needed the khan's patent to rule. In the 1300s the princes of Moscow won that title, and the Grand Duchy of Moscow took the old principality's place.
